videos.title: This Filament Destroys Your 3D Printer Nozzle ⚠️ #shorts
videos.description:
Glow-in-the-dark filament is packed with strontium aluminate particles – that's what makes it glow, but it's also abrasive. Print after print it grinds away a normal brass nozzle: the hole gets wider and you get under-extrusion and messy prints. The fix: a hardened steel nozzle for glow, carbon fiber and other abrasive filaments.

Source: https://qidi3d.com/blogs/print-lab/glow-in-dark-filament-ti

videos.description:

videos.title: Your USB-C Cable Has a Secret Chip 🔌 #shorts
videos.description:
Many USB-C cables hide a tiny e-marker chip in the plug. It tells the charger what the cable can safely handle – current, voltage and data speed. Without one, a cable is treated as 3 A, so 60 W at most. With an e-marker it can carry 5 A: up to 100 W, and up to 240 W with the newest USB Power Delivery standard.

Source: https://us.ktcplay.com/blogs/technology-hub/usb-c-cable-e-marker-chips

#shorts

videos.title: Your Bank Card Is a Computer (With No Battery) 💳 #shorts
videos.description:
That golden square on your bank card is a secure microcontroller – a tiny computer with its own processor and memory. A contactless card has no battery: an antenna coil inside picks up power from the reader's field, typically within about 4 cm. And for every payment the chip creates a unique one-time code, so copied data can't simply be reused.

Source: https://www.analog.com/en/resources/app-note

videos.title: What Happens When the Last Bitcoin Is Mined? #shorts
videos.description:
The last bitcoin is expected around the year 2140. After that, miners will be paid only through transaction fees. And bitcoin won't run out of small change: one bitcoin is 100 million satoshis. Will fees alone keep the network secure? That's one of Bitcoin's biggest open questions.

Source: https://river.com/learn/what-will-happen-after-all-bitcoin-mined/

videos.title: 12 Words That Control All Your Crypto 🔐 #shorts
videos.description:
A seed phrase is 12 or 24 words from a list of exactly 2,048 words. Your coins live on the blockchain – the seed phrase creates the keys that control them. Guessing it is practically impossible, but anyone who sees it owns your coins. Write it on paper or metal, never type it into a website, and never share it.

Source: https://btc.network/learn/what-is-a-seed-phrase

#shorts #crypto #bitcoin #sec

videos.title: She Got a 3D Printed Titanium Jaw #shorts
videos.description:
In 2011 in the Netherlands, an 83-year-old woman received a new lower jaw printed from titanium powder – a laser fused it layer by layer, 33 layers per millimeter. Designed from her scans, it's recognized as the first 3D printed complete lower jaw implant.

Source: https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/107376-first-3d-printed-complete-lower-jaw-implant

videos.title: Adidas 3D Printed the Sole of This Shoe 👟 #shorts
videos.description:
The Adidas Futurecraft 4D (2017) has a 3D printed lattice midsole made with Carbon's light-based process: light hardens a liquid resin and the part grows out of the liquid. A lattice lets every zone feel different – softer in the heel, firmer in the front – all in one part.

Source: https://techcrunch.com/2017/04/07/adidas-latest-3d-printed-shoe-puts-mass-production-within-sight/

#shorts #3dprint

videos.title: Robots 3D Printed a Steel Bridge #shorts
videos.description:
Welding robots built this bridge layer by layer out of molten steel – about 12 meters long and around 6 tonnes. Sensors measured how it moved as people walked across, and Queen Máxima opened it over a canal in Amsterdam in July 2021.

Sources: https://www.euronews.com/2021/07/16/the-world-s-first-3d-printed-steel-bridge-has-opened-in-amsterdam · https://www.guinnessworldrecords.com/world-records/6
